subject: rstan plotting functions fail with soon to be released new ggplot2 version (2.2.0)

messages.author: 2ffa956ce2411d70
messages.subject: rstan plotting functions fail with soon to be released new ggplot2 version (2.2.0)
parts:
Dear all,

I just wanted to inform you that the rstan plotting functions seem to fail with the latest development version of ggplot2. This version is scheduled to be released in November: https://blog.rstudio.org/2016/09/30/ggplot2-2-2-0-coming-soon/

To see the problem run the following code in R:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("hadley/ggplot2")
require(rstan)
example("read_stan_csv")
stan_plot(fit)
stan_trace(fit)

The first plotting function produces:
Error in if (e1$inherit.blank) return(e2) else return(e1) : 
  argument is of length zero

The second one produces:
Error in `[.unit`(padding, 4) : index out of bounds ('unit' subsetting)

I have already reported it on ggplot's github (although this might be the better place): https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/1824

Cheers,
Henrik

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan plotting functions fail with soon to be released new ggplot2 version (2.2.0)
parts:
Yeah so the recent ggplot2 release broke backwards compatibility (again). The develop branch of rstan should already be compatible if you want to use that, but our release schedule is a bit behind Hadley's. Our bayesplot package (which has even more functionality for plotting than what's currently in rstan) is also already fully compatible with the new ggplot2 and can be installed from GitHub (stan-dev/bayesplot). A CRAN release of that package is also coming soon. 

Jonah
